implementation_statement: The Operations Manager requests accounts; the MSP creates suite and device accounts; the Operations Manager creates core, admin console, wire portal, and LOS users. evidence: Core role profiles; admin console role report

implementation_statement: The wire portal enforces maker-checker: the Senior MSR keys, and the Operations Manager or the Accounting and Compliance Officer approves with a hardware token. With 7 staff, the Operations Manager also administers core users and approves wires; the independent assessor and the board's annual report compensate.
evidence: Wire portal role report; token assignment list

implementation_statement: Staff have no local administrator rights on computers (MSP policy). Gap: all 3 MSRs hold the core supervisor override profile so they can cover for each other.
evidence: MSP endpoint policy; core role profiles

evidence: Core processor SOC 2 report; vendor documentation

implementation_statement: The MSP sets a 10-minute screen lock. Gap: the 4 teller stations are exempt at staff request.
The core and online banking end idle sessions (vendor settings).

Staff have no remote access to the core (office IP allowlist). The MSP reaches every computer through its remote management tool and administers the cloud tenant. Gap: no list of MSP technicians with access and no evidence of MFA on the MSP tool.

implementation_statement: A monthly review checklist (core exception and user reports, admin console changes to member contact data and payees, wire portal activity, suite sign-ins and mailbox rules) starts 2026-10-31.
Core and wire portal records are kept by the vendors. Gap: suite sign-in logs are kept only for the plan's default period, shorter than one year.
The Supervisory Committee engaged an independent IT audit consultant for the 2026 control assessment (P07), to be repeated yearly.
The MSP changes firewall, endpoint, and tenant settings on request or on its own schedule. Gap: no record of approval by the credit union for changes that affect member information systems.
The MSP keeps a device list. Gap: no inventory of SaaS services and of where member information is stored (the shared mailbox and imaging server were not on any list).

The 2019 business continuity plan will be rewritten from the P05 BIA, with offline teller mode, the alternate wire procedure, hurricane steps, the catastrophic act report (748.1(b)), and the vital records log (Part 749). Due 2026-12-31.
First tests: imaging server restore by the MSP (2026-09-30), alternate phone wire with the corporate credit union (2026-10-31), and a tabletop of the P08 runbook (2026-11-30).
